name: Grove at Cottonwood
award: 2024 Federal 9% and state housing tax credits (Round One)
headline: The Broomfield Housing Alliance and BlueLine Development built the Grove at Cottonwood, a 40-unit, neuro-inclusive rental community at 30% to 60% AMI in Broomfield's Northmoor neighborhood, with 10 units set aside for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities; it won 2024 Round One 9% and state credits and opened in 2026.
why_it_matters: It is a finished, small-scale model for I/DD housing under the tax credit program: a housing authority's own land, 10 Section 811 vouchers from the Division of Housing and referral agreements with I/DD service agencies, delivered in about a year of construction.

status.label: Completed; certificate of occupancy July 2026; leasing up (grand opening 2026-09-02)
status.detail: The project's construction page reports substantial completion and a certificate of occupancy in July 2026. Denver7 reported the grand opening on 2026-09-02, with 10 residents moved in, 10 more preparing to move in and 20 units still available.

next_step: Watch for full lease-up and for the recorded CHFA land use restriction agreement and placed-in-service year.

background.text: Origin: the idea came from parents seeking housing for adult children with I/DD and was developed with a CHFA Small-Scale Housing Technical Assistance Grant awarded in 2022. It is the Broomfield Housing Alliance's first development.

Under Section 811 rules the 10 I/DD units are filled through referral agencies, and the other 30 units cannot be limited to people with disabilities, so the community is mixed. An alliance-employed resident concierge drives a property van and coordinates services, in part because the market study found low walk and transit scores.

Local approvals: the narrative says council approved a rezoning, right-of-way vacation, PUD plan, final plat and site development plan in January 2024. Broomfield's council video index lists the public hearing on the Grove at Cottonwood Filing No. 1 rezoning and right-of-way vacation (second reading) on 2024-02-13.

Neighbor concerns about density, height, traffic and parking led to dropping a through street, lowering building height, stepping density down toward single-family homes to the east and adding parking. Broomfield code required a Good Neighbor Policy; the alliance held neighbor meetings on 2024-10-21, 2024-11-06 and 2025-01-27.
CHFA granted a cost basis override for the site and design costs; the application asked for no other waiver.

Construction: groundbreaking in the week of 2025-07-11; foundations and utilities by September 2025; main building dried in by January 2026; exteriors mostly complete by May 2026; certificate of occupancy July 2026.
Opening: the grand opening was held 2026-09-02. The leasing page says the interest list is longer than expected.

discrepancies.text: CHFA and the application narrative give the address as 1354 Cottonwood Street, while the owner's Good Neighbor Policy lists 1355, 1374 and 1394 Cottonwood Street and BlueLine's community page uses 1355 Cottonwood Street.

The application narrative says council approved the rezoning, right-of-way vacation and related plans in January 2024, while Broomfield's council video index shows the rezoning and right-of-way vacation second-reading public hearing on 2024-02-13.
